concept.name: Pattern day trader rule
concept.definition: The FINRA margin rule regime under which a customer who executes four or more day trades within five business days in a margin account (a day trade being the purchase and sale, or sale and purchase, of the same security on the same day) is designated a 'pattern day trader' and becomes subject to special margin requirements, historically a $25,000 minimum equity requirement.
concept.intuition: If you day trade frequently with borrowed money, regulators make you keep a serious cash cushion in the account so a bad day doesn't sink the broker too.
concept.mechanics: Day trades are counted per margin account across a rolling five-business-day window; once designated, the account historically had to maintain at least $25,000 in equity and was limited in day-trading buying power, with violations triggering restrictions to cash-only trading. FINRA has since adopted new intraday margin requirements replacing the former day-trading margin requirements, so the precise margin mechanics are in transition.
concept.formula: Designation trigger: day trades >= 4 within 5 business days in a margin account; classic requirement: minimum account equity >= $25,000.
concept.failure_modes: The five-day counting window and per-account application confuse retail traders, who inadvertently trigger the designation; the rule has also been criticized for pushing small accounts toward options, offshore brokers, or cash-account settlement workarounds (good faith violations) rather than reducing risk.
concept.misconceptions: The rule is a margin requirement, not a ban on day trading, and it does not apply to cash accounts (which face separate free-riding/settlement constraints); holding a position overnight and selling the next day is not a day trade.
concept.example: A trader buys and sells AAPL three times on Monday and does one more round trip on Thursday in her margin account; with four day trades in five business days she is designated a pattern day trader and must meet the applicable minimum equity rules to keep day trading.
